title: Traffic Temporal Orchestrator for Safe Model Rollouts
creator: Sophie Nguyen
description: We need a unified, policy-driven orchestrator that expresses time-based and metric-based traffic schedules for model rollouts. Current canary mechanisms are ad-hoc, embedded in individual services, and lack composable guardrails for shadow probing, A/B splits, and automatic rollback conditions. This ticket scopes a first implementation: a Temporal Orchestrator service + policy schema that lets PM/Platform define multi-step traffic plans (percent, duration, probes) with circuit-breakers, SLA-aware pauses, and automated rollback triggers. Goals: (1) enable engineers to declare rollout plans in a single YAML/JSON policy, (2) integrate with Console for visualization and manual overrides, (3) expose safe defaults and opt-in aggressive strategies for advanced users.
acceptance_criteria: Policy schema v1 defined and validated in open PR
Orchestrator service implements time-based step executor and percent router hooks
Guardrail engine supports threshold-based pause and automatic rollback rules
Shadow traffic routing available as a switch on policies
Console shows per-step timeline, projected traffic curve, and live telemetry
E2E tests for canary -> full rollout with simulated errors and auto-rollback
implementation_notes: Architecture: lightweight service (k8s deployment) subscribes to rollout config store. It emits scheduled dispatches to Router service which adjusts traffic splits via the existing route API. Guardrails evaluate metrics from Telemetry (Grafana/Prometheus) through a small rules engine; on violation it triggers an automated rollback operation using the Rollback API. We considered embedding scheduling inside Router but rejected it to keep Router stateless and minimize blast radius. Policy format is YAML-first with a JSON schema for validation. We will reuse the existing rollout history table in Postgres for auditability. Trade-offs: separate service adds operational overhead but keeps rollout logic decoupled and easier to version. For low-latency emergencies, provide a direct toggle on the Console for immediate full rollback.
comments: 2026-02-25 - Sophie Nguyen: Filed initial ticket after post-mortem from ENG-76328 incident where ad-hoc rollout contributed to a latency spike for a subset of customers. Goal is to centralize scheduling and guardrails.

2026-02-27 - Marco Silva: Spike completed — implemented prototype scheduler that emits step events. Found race where Router updates could be applied out-of-order during rapid step changes; added versioned rollout token to mitigate.

2026-03-01 - Priya Menon (PM): Reviewed policy schema. Requested explicit fields for 'shadow_fraction' and 'probe_profile' to support long-tail experiments and canary probes (latency p99, error-rate, model-quality metric).

2026-03-02 - Design review (Aisha Khan): Console wireframes approved with minor tweaks — need clearer UX for manual pause vs. rollback; recommended confirming color semantics for 'paused' vs 'failed' steps.

2026-03-03 - Security (Ethan Clarke): Asked for threat model for policy storage; recommending KMS encryption at rest for rollout secrets and RBAC enforcement on who can trigger/approve rollouts. Added as dependency.

2026-03-04 - Marco Silva: Implemented guardrail rule engine with Prometheus query adapter. Observed noisy metric flapping around thresholds in staging; added 3-step debounce window before auto-rollback to avoid oscillation.
2026-03-05 - Sophie Nguyen: QA found that shadow routing doubled request counts for some customers during A/B tests. Added requirement to surface expected request multiplier in Console and docs.
notes_for_reviews: Please focus review on: (1) policy schema completeness for combined shadow + A/B scenarios, (2) guardrail debounce logic and default thresholds, (3) RBAC surface and audit trail format. Known limitation: model-quality metrics require upstream evaluators; we will provide a fallback of latency/error-rate until those are standard.
ci_steps: unit tests for scheduler and rule engine
integration test: simulated Prometheus metrics + orchestrator -> router handoff
e2e canary flow with synthetic traffic harness
security scans for secret material in configs
risks: Operator error: users may author rollouts that escalate traffic too quickly — mitigate with conservative defaults and approval gates
Metric quality: poor signal leads to false rollbacks — mitigate by allowing custom probe profiles and manual confirmations
Operational overhead: additional service to run; will include resource limits and auto-scaling policy
